Reagovala tak na varování rozvědky před možnými ruskými sabotážemi a vpády přes hranice.

Článek
„V reakci na hrozbu sabotáží posílily polské bezpečnostní složky ochranu hranic,“ vysvětlila stanice přesuny na polské straně hranice s ruskou Kaliningradskou oblastí. Velení polských bezpečnostních sil vyslalo do Podlaského a Varmijsko-mazurského vojvodství posily, včetně příslušníků polské speciální jednotky GROM, dalších příslušníků pohraniční stráže a policejních protiteroristických jednotek.
Podle polského premiéra Donalda Tuska se posily aktivovaly, když pohraničníci v noci na úterý zaznamenali…

shrnuti: Norway is deploying NASAMS sensors in Kirkenes and reinforcing its military presence with over 30 soldiers to detect drones near the Russian border.

Norway deploys drone detection system near Russian border | Ukrainska Pravda
The Norwegian flag. Photo: Getty Images
The Norwegian Armed Forces are deploying an aerial surveillance system in the town of Kirkenes, near the Russian border, to detect drones that stray off course at an early stage.
Source: a press release by the Norwegian government, as reported by European Pravda
Details: The Norwegian Air Force is deploying specialised NASAMS sensors, while the military garrison in the region will be reinforced by more than 30 soldiers.

The government noted that the measures are preventive and are not linked to any specific new threat.
The sensors are designed to detect drones, warn of their presence and provide a comprehensive picture of all activity in the airspace over border areas.

No drone crashes were reported.

titulek: British police arrest senior U.S. Army soldier near Gloucester on suspicion of spying for Russia
titulekPuvodni: British police arrest senior U.S. Army soldier near Gloucester on suspicion of spying for Russia
shrnuti: British police have arrested a senior U.S. Army soldier on suspicion of working for Russian intelligence. The 41-year-old was detained on Tuesday near Gloucester and taken to London, where he is being held at a police station.

British police arrest senior U.S. Army soldier near Gloucester on suspicion of spying for Russia
November 10, 2026, 9:29 pm
Source: NBC News
British police have arrested a senior U.S. Army soldier on suspicion of working for Russian intelligence. The 41-year-old was detained on Tuesday near Gloucester and taken to London, where he is being held at a police station.
FBI Director Kash Patel called the arrest “important” and said it “involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies.”
Noting the investigation is ongoing, he added that the FBI “has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners.”
The soldier had access to sensitive information, said General Sean Stinchon, the commanding general of U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command.

Garry Kasparov, a Russian opposition figure and the 13th world chess champion, canceled a trip to Berlin after security services warned of a possible threat to his life, the German tabloid Bild reported.
Kasparov was scheduled to speak at Berlin Freedom Week. Instead, he recorded a video address for participants, in which he acknowledged reports that Russia was trying to kill him. He said security professionals had strongly advised him against traveling to Berlin because the trip would be an unjustifiable risk under the circumstances.
Kasparov also criticized European authorities for not doing enough to counter the Russian government, accusing European politicians of letting Europe become a playground for Vladimir Putin. If Putin could reach him there, Kasparov warned, he could reach anyone.

shrnuti: Two Ukrainian citizens, ages 24 and 25, have been arrested in Poland on suspicion of espionage and sabotage on behalf of Russian intelligence services, said Tomasz Siemoniak, the Polish minister who coordinates the country’s intelligence services.

Skip to main content
Poland arrests two Ukrainians suspected of spying and sabotage for Russia
November 10, 2026, 5:09 pm
Source: Internal Security Agency of Poland (ABW)
Two Ukrainian citizens, ages 24 and 25, have been arrested in Poland on suspicion of espionage and sabotage on behalf of Russian intelligence services, said Tomasz Siemoniak, the Polish minister who coordinates the country’s intelligence services.
Investigators allege that the two photographed critical infrastructure and military facilities in Poland and set cars on fire. They replaced vehicle license plates with plates from Ukrainian military vehicles to deflect suspicion. They were paid for these tasks, including in cryptocurrency.
Poland’s Internal Security Agency said both suspects have been ordered held in custody for three months. They face sentences ranging from 10 years to life in prison, the agency said.

PARIS — Tehran denied accusations by Paris that it was behind the recent series of cyberattacks targeting supermarket refrigerators in France, calling the claims “baseless and biased.”
The Iranian foreign ministry said in a statement Tuesday that it “strongly condemns” France’s “worn-out policy of making accusations against Iran.”
French Minister of Foreign Affairs Jean-Noël Barrot on Monday said Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps was responsible for the “unprecedented” cyberattacks against several supermarket chains last month. On Tuesday, Barrot said Paris would not “rule out anything” in its response to the attacks, which affected 700 food distribution sites.

A freight train derailed in northwestern Russia’s Arkhangelsk region following the collapse of a railroad bridge, Russian Railways and local officials said Tuesday, causing disruptions to passenger rail service along the affected track.
Arkhangelsk region Governor Alexander Tsybulsky said the accident took place around 5:10 a.m. Moscow time. He said part of a railroad bridge over the Viled River collapsed, leading several freight cars to derail.
Tsybulsky said officials were coordinating an emergency response effort. No one was injured in the accident.
At least eight long-distance passenger trains traveling between major cities — including Moscow and St. Petersburg — were left stranded following the derailment.
Russian Railways said it sent buses to the area to transport passengers further to their destinations. The company said repair crews were also dispatched to the bridge but did not say how long it expected the affected…

One of France's last Resistance heroes from World War Two has died at the age of 104. Solange Alexandre was also a rare woman who, with her future husband, created and commanded her own unit of anti-German fighters.
After serving as a Resistance courier from 1941, three years later she founded the Pas-de-Boeuf network near the town of Ruillé-sur-Loir.
With some 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and, after the Allied landings in Normandy on D-Day in 1944, joined the fight against the occupying German forces.
President Emmanuel Macron was among many to pay tribute to Alexandre, after her death was announced at a nursing home in Le Mans.
"She said she only ever did her duty. But her duty was our freedom. France will never forget. Thank you," Macron posted on social media.

Armenian law enforcement authorities have taken two Russian soldiers into custody after they were accused of assaulting a Ukrainian man, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty’s (RFE/RL) Armenian service reported Monday.
The alleged assault took place about a month ago in the city of Gyumri, which hosts Russia’s 102nd Military Base.
Armenian investigators told RFE/RL that they launched a criminal probe into the assault allegations and had ordered a forensic medical examination after the Ukrainian man, identified as Dmytro Samuelenko, filed a police report.
The detention marks a departure from decades of legal precedent, where Russian military personnel accused of committing crimes in Gyumri would be held at the Russian military base.

Skip to main content
Advertisement
PARIS — French Minister of Foreign Affairs Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran was behind the recent series of “unprecedented” cyberattacks on refrigerators in several major supermarket chains in the country last month.
“Thanks to the outstanding work of the government departments, I am able to confirm that responsibility for this attack lies with the Iranian Revolutionary Guards,” Barrot told reporters Monday at a G7 meeting in Paris. “We will impose sanctions at European level against those responsible.”
Barrot said that 700 food distribution sites in France were impacted in the cyberattack. French prosecutors said shortly after that they were opening an investigation into the hacks.
Though Barrot was only referring to the incidents reported in France, grocery stores across Europe and even French blood banks have been targeted by hackers in recent days. Cyber experts had previously raised concerns that the attacks may have been part of Russia’s ongoing hybrid warfare against Europe, though the Kremlin has denied any involvement.

Ukrainian drones struck the Leningrad region overnight on November 9, and 113 of them were shot down, Governor Alexander Drozdenko said.
Drozdenko said “there have been instances of drone hits” in an industrial zone in Kirishi. He said “fragments” also hit an apartment in Kirishi and the roof of an apartment building in Vsevolozhsk, without providing further details.
Update. Drozdenko later confirmed that drones struck an oil refinery in Kirishi, where a fire broke out. In Vsevolozhsk, a woman died after “falling of debris” from a drone hit the roof of a house. Astra, an independent Telegram channel, analyzed videos from Kirishi and reported that the Kirishinefteorgsintez oil refinery — a Surgutneftegas subsidiary and one of the largest refineries in Russia — was on fire.
Ukrainian monitoring channels also reported the fire at the Kirishi plant.

The life Vasilij Kovacs knew ended with a bang. It was late afternoon on March 1, 2025, when an armored vehicle smashed through the metal gate of the old farmhouse where he lived southeast of the Latvian capital, Riga.
Masked men emerged with their guns drawn. They belonged to Latvia’s State Security Service, the country’s counterintelligence agency. The officers searched the property, seizing several mobile phones, SIM cards and documents, along with a pistol with its serial number filed off, a bayonet from an AK-47 and a cellphone jammer, according to a search report later filed by the authorities. They arrested Kovacs, a Ukrainian man in his 60s who has lived in Latvia for more than 30 years.
In March, Kovacs was transferred to stand trial in Lithuania, where he is accused of planning terrorist attacks, alongside four alleged accomplices. Five others face trial in Warsaw. 07.11.2026 10.16
Online seit heute, 10.16 Uhr
Nach einer Serie von Bombendrohungen gegen Flüge ermitteln die italienischen Behörden wegen des Verdachts der Störung der öffentlichen Ordnung. Verfahren wurden bereits in Mailand, Rom und Busto Arsizio eingeleitet, hieß es heute. Die Ermittlungen werden von der Nationalen Anti-Mafia- und Anti-Terrorismus-Staatsanwaltschaft koordiniert. Die Ermittler schließen eine europaweite Koordination der Aktionen nicht aus.
Internationale Kooperationskanäle wurden aktiviert, um die Server und IP-Adressen zu identifizieren, über die die E-Mails verschickt wurden. Erste Hinweise deuteten darauf hin, dass die Nachrichten über kompromittierte E-Mail-Konten oder Dienste zur Anonymisierung der Absender, darunter Proton Mail, versandt worden sein könnten.
Auch die europäische Polizeibehörde Europol steht nach Angaben aus Italien bereit, die nationalen Ermittlungsbehörden zu unterstützen. Für die kommende Woche ist zudem in Brüssel ein Treffen der Luftsicherheitsexperten aus den 27 EU-Mitgliedsstaaten geplant. Dabei sollen mögliche…

Senior U.S. trade and health officials are expected to meet with the German government in mid-November for talks on its drug pricing policies, a German government spokesperson confirmed to POLITICO.
The talks come as Germany races to avoid U.S. tariffs if it does not reach an agreement with Washington — after the Trump administration launched a trade investigation into Berlin’s pricing policies in June.
The Trump administration alleges Germany underpays for new drugs, leaving the U.S. to shoulder a disproportionate share of the global cost of developing innovative medicines.

'Too early to draw conclusions' as bomb threat hoaxes target European countries
Issued on: 06/11/2026 - 14:48
Share
Several Irish media outlets reported receiving bomb threats on Friday as a wave of hoax alerts that had so far mainly targeted airlines continued across Europe, with more than a dozen new flights affected. No explosives have been found in any of the incidents so far. European authorities are scrambling to identify the sources of the threats, as FRANCE 24's Brussels correspondent Dave Keating reports.

Článek
Počet obětí pondělního ruského útoku leteckými pumami na středisko humanitární pomoci v obci Komyšuvacha v Záporožské oblasti vzrostl na 53. V pátek to oznámil velitel regionální vojenské správy Mychajlo Semikin na telegram u. Státní služba pro mimořádné situace (DSNS) o něco dříve informovala o 50 mrtvých. Za letošek jde o ruský útok s největším počtem obětí na životech.
„Na místě tragédie pátým dnem pokračují pátrací a záchranné práce,“ uvedl Semikin. Vyjádřil soustrast blízkým obětí a poděkoval záchranářům. Kolik osob se dále pohřešuje, v pátek nezveřejnil.
V uplynulých dnech úřady uváděly, že se pohřešuje několik desítek lidí.…

A fresh wave of bomb threats has disrupted air traffic across Europe but the affected planes landed safely and searches revealed no explosive devices.
The latest alerts affected at least 18 flights to or from Bulgaria , Czechia, France, Italy, Hungary, Cyprus, Romania, the UK and Portugal. Danish police investigated a threat against Copenhagen airport but the airport said it was operating normally.

shrnuti: Scores of flights across Europe have received bomb threats this week, but no explosives have been found so far.

vyrez.text:
Russian extremist group denies sending hoax bomb threats - BBC News
Image source, Reuters
Image caption, Passengers on this Aer Lingus flight to Rome were diverted to a military base in France after a bomb threat
By Sarah Rainsford Southern and Eastern Europe correspondent
Published
1 hour ago
The "Male State", an extremist misogynistic group named in this week's hoax bomb threats to Italian airports, has denied any link to the false warnings causing flight disruption across Europe .
The comments to the BBC came as reports of more bomb scares to airlines began appearing, including on a Ryanair flight from Rome to Lisbon and a Wizz Air flight from Prague to Rome which was diverted to Venice.
Bomb threats were also reported to a number of high-profile Irish media organisations on Friday, prompting evacuations and a statement from the Irish government suggesting a "co-ordinated campaign of disruption".
Replying to the BBC Russian Service, an account on Telegram - one of several linked to the so-called "Male State" and its founder Vladislav Pozdnyakov - mocked any suggestion the group was involved in emailing the threats.

On 4 November, the State Police detained two Belarusian nationals – a train driver and his assistant – on suspicion of large-scale smuggling. The men threw several packets of illegal cigarettes from a moving train.
A total of 140,000 “NZ Gold” cigarettes bearing Belarusian excise stamps were seized.
The police established that the packets of illegal cigarettes had been thrown from a moving train that had entered Daugavpils from Belarus.
On 6 November, the State Police will ask the court to impose a custodial measure on both detainees. Criminal proceedings have been initiated for smuggling, if committed by an organised group, or for smuggling on a large scale.

Zbrojařská a strojírenská skupina Czechoslovak Group (CSG) podnikatele Michala Strnada se dostala mezi firmy, které mohou usilovat o zakázky na modernizace sedmi amerických muničních závodů dohromady za až 4,2 miliardy dolarů (91,5 miliardy Kč).
Jednotlivé projekty bude americká armáda v pětiletém rámcovém programu MATOC zadávat samostatně podle výsledků soutěží. ČTK to v pátek oznámil mluvčí CSG Andrej Čírtek.
Rámcový kontrakt americké armády CSG získala prostřednictvím své americké společnosti MSM North America. Modernizace muničních závodů ve vlastnictví státu, které provozují soukromé společnosti, zahrnuje rozšíření výroby a zavádění moderních…
